variants.headline: The Congress takes up {{count|new proposal|new proposals}}
body: The World Congress agenda now carries {{count|new proposal|new proposals}}, and {{proposal}} leads the list. Clerks are still copying the drafts for the delegations. In the taverns where envoys lodge, the talk is all about who wrote each one and what it will cost to oppose it.

variants.headline: One new matter for the world's chamber
body: A single new proposal has reached the World Congress: {{proposal}}. It waits for the delegates at their next sitting. The clerks who carried the papers will not say who asked for it, which has done more for the gossip than any speech could.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our name is on the agenda
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! A proposal of ours now sits before the World Congress. Stop a delegate in the square and make him tell you what we have asked of the world. It bears our name, and every capital will read it!

variants.headline: New business for the delegates
body: Notice to the delegations: the World Congress has new business before it, {{proposal}} on the agenda, and will take it up in due course. Delegates should arrive with instructions in order and arguments rehearsed. Careful preparation separates a serious delegation from a noisy one.

variants.headline: The Congress docket grows
body: Fresh proposals on the Congress docket: {{count}}.
Leading the list: {{proposal}}.

variants.headline: The Congress votes a measure down
body: A proposal has failed in the World Congress. Its sponsors stood in the aisle with the draft in hand and watched the count close against them. The measure is finished for now, and its authors must decide whether to bring it back.

variants.headline: Delegates reject {{resolution}}
body: Delegates have voted {{resolution}} down. Nothing in the statute book changes, and a speech polished for a season died in a single morning. Its author was last seen folding his notes on the chamber steps.

variants.headline: A repeal refused, and the law stands
body: The chamber has kept one of its own laws on the books. Supporters of repeal expected the numbers to hold, and the count did not bear them out. They will need a new session and more allies before the question comes back.

variants.headline: The chamber turns our proposal away
body: Our delegates carried a proposal to the World Congress, and it came home in pieces. The vote showed exactly how many friends we have in that hall. The {{terms.civic.government}} should count them, then go out and find more before the next session.

variants.headline: The Congress carries a measure
body: A proposal has passed in the World Congress, and the law of the world has shifted with it. Clerks were still at their copying when messengers began arriving for texts to carry home. Delegations that voted for it are already explaining what they won.

variants.headline: The Congress enacts {{resolution}}
body: The Congress has enacted {{resolution}}. When the count was done, a correspondent watched a clerk pin the adopted text beside the motion so that any reader could compare the two. The clerk's pencil marks, he said, were the most honest account in the building.

variants.headline: The Congress strikes {{resolution}} from the books
body: The Congress has repealed {{resolution}}. Word went out to the dispatch desks, where the old instructions were pulled from the shelves and stacked for the fire. Not every household will be sorry to see them go.

variants.headline: Hear it! Our measure has carried the Congress
body: Our delegates put it forward, and the chamber has carried it! Hear it at the gate and in the market: the count came down on our side! Run ahead of the couriers, and let every town in the realm hear what we have won!

variants.headline: The World Congress has sanctioned us
body: The chamber's new law is {{resolution}}, and the nation it names is ours. At the harbor, a shipping clerk has read the notice twice and set aside a cargo he meant to send. The counting houses will have the sums worked out before the {{terms.civic.government}} has finished reading the page.

variants.headline: Hear it! The Congress has set its hand against us
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! The chamber has written {{resolution}} into its law, and the ink is aimed at us! They have marked us, but they have not muzzled us! Stone walls do not outlast the nations that build them!

variants.headline: Tell merchants what the sanction stops
body: A sanction now stands against us, and the docks will feel it before the palace does. A merchant fitting out a ship needs to know which ports will still take his cargo, and he needs to know tonight. Tell him while the ship is at the quay, not after the sails are up. Our {{terms.civic.government}} should post the terms where working people can read them.

variants.headline: The sanction, and the silence around it
body: {{resolution}} now sits in the chamber's books, and it has our name on it. Our envoys will walk into every foreign room carrying that mark, and they know it. No ministry has offered a route out of it, and none has named a price it would pay. A government with a plan would have told us by now.

variants.headline: The World Congress sits in {{turnsUntil}}
body: The World Congress is expected to sit again in {{turnsUntil}}. Delegations are packing their instructions and counting the favors they can still call in. Clerks at the chamber have begun clearing the galleries, and the corridors smell of fresh ink.

variants.headline: The World Congress sits at any moment
body: The chamber may be called to order at any moment. The agenda lies ready on the table, the galleries are packed, and half the world is waiting on the sound of the gavel.

variants.headline: Notice: {{league}} to convene
body: Delegates to {{league}} are reminded that the chamber sits in {{turnsUntil}}. Bring your instructions, and bring them settled. A delegation that arrives still arguing among itself will be heard as silence.

variants.headline: Countdown to the session
body: Next sitting in {{turnsUntil}}.
Proposals already piling up: {{count}}.

variants.headline: The days when the bargains are priced
body: With {{turnsUntil}} before the chamber opens, the bargaining has already started in the corridors. A vote is won before it is cast, by whoever has collected the most promises and remembered the most debts. Our delegation should be out visiting, not waiting to be visited. A seat at that table is worth more than a speech at it.

variants.headline: The World Congress convenes on the next turn
body: The World Congress convenes tomorrow. The delegations are filing in, the galleries have gone still, and the clerk is clearing his throat to read the agenda. Whatever is decided there will bind every nation in the hall.

variants.headline: Notice to the delegations: {{league}} sits
body: {{league}} meets tomorrow, and the whole town knows it! Settle your instructions tonight, and count your promises twice. In that chamber, a debt forgotten is a vote lost.

variants.headline: World Congress to hear {{count|proposal|proposals}} at its next session
body: Tomorrow the World Congress takes up {{count|proposal|proposals}}. At a schoolhouse in the capital, the oldest pupils are debating the same list and voting by show of hands. Their teacher says she asks each one to defend a choice. She would like to ask our delegates the same question.

variants.headline: Hear it! One matter before the world's chamber
body: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}}! Tomorrow the chamber votes, and a single proposal stands before it! A single sheet, a single count, and every household in the realm lives with the result! Come to the square and hear it as it falls!

variants.headline: Our votes in the Congress change
body: Our delegation now commands {{votes|vote|votes}} in the World Congress, where {{previous}} answered before. At the lodging, the usher has chalked the new count on the slate by the door. The old number is still visible under it, if anyone cares to look.

variants.headline: Our voice in the Congress grows
body: The chamber now counts {{votes|vote|votes}} behind our name, against {{previous}} at the last tally. Delegations that ignored us last season will find a reason to call this week. In that hall, arithmetic is the only argument that closes.

variants.headline: Our voice in the Congress shrinks
body: Our standing in the World Congress has dropped from {{previous|vote|votes}} to {{votes|vote|votes}}. Somewhere between those two numbers are the delegations that stopped answering us. The foreign minister should name them, and say what he means to offer before the next ballot.

variants.headline: Voting opens in the World Congress
body: Voting is under way in the World Congress. Delegates are called up one at a time, and the galleries have stopped talking. The world's next rules hang on a tally that will not finish until evening.

variants.headline: Notice from {{league}}: the vote is open
body: {{league}} has opened its vote, and the delegates are at the ballot. The count will be published once the last name is called. The world is asked to keep its temper until then. Every delegation there will need the others before the year is out.

variants.headline: Voting day in the world's chamber
body: The World Congress votes tonight on {{count|proposal|proposals}}. In that hall, second place buys nothing. The cloakrooms are empty because every deal worth making was made hours ago.

variants.headline: The Congress vote is live
body: The Congress is voting right now.
The ballot carries {{count|proposal|proposals}}. Yours is probably not on it, but you will live under whatever passes.

variants.headline: The Congress sets a world ideology
body: The world's assembly has adopted {{resolution}} and written it into the common law. In a rival capital, the magistrate's office worked late, copying the new text into the city's book of statutes. The printers there will have it on every doorstep by morning.

variants.headline: Our ideology carries the world
body: Our ideology now stands as {{resolution}}, and the world's chamber has voted it into law. In that hall, a shared creed buys more than a signed treaty and lasts about as long as the goodwill behind it. Our delegates should put that credit to work while the count is fresh.

variants.headline: A creed not ours is crowned
body: The Congress has crowned {{resolution}} as the world's creed, and the name is not ours. No vote in a marble hall can warm a shrine or answer a prayer. The faithful should keep their lamps lit, and the {{terms.civic.government}} should state plainly which altars it means to protect.

variants.headline: Which delegations clapped, and which didn't
body: When the clerk read out {{resolution}}, the gallery watched for the first delegation to clap, and the second, and the ones that kept their hands still. That small performance was the real business of the day. On the wharves, the stevedores have their own test for a creed, and it comes due on payday.

variants.headline: A world project before the Congress
body: {{project}} is before the World Congress, and every nation is weighing what it will put into the work. A foreman at the shipyard has begun listing which men he can spare and for how long. The biggest contribution earns the biggest reward, and he means to be ready.

variants.headline: What a share in {{project}} will cost
body: Every delegation is asking the same question about {{project}}: what will a leading share cost us, and what will it return? The chamber pays best for the greatest contribution. That payment comes out of workshops and fields, where the hands are already spoken for. A nation with a full order book should count the loss before it counts the prize.

variants.headline: Trade halls eye work on {{project}}
body: News from the Congress tonight: {{project}} is open, and the work will go to the nations that commit to it. Back home, a foreman at the machine shop is already asking whether his crew will get a share. "I have good hands going idle next week," he says. "Tell me before the week is out."

variants.headline: A blank line under {{project}}
body: The sign painter down the street has lettered {{project}} across the top of a fresh board. A passerby asks him what belongs in the empty space below. "Our country's name," he says. "I am waiting to see whether we earn the right to paint it."

variants.headline: The Congress names a world religion
body: The World Congress has blessed {{resolution}} and set it above every other faith. A shrine keeper at the edge of town read the notice and put it under a stone on the counter. He lit the lamps at the usual hour, and this time only a handful of neighbors came.

variants.headline: Our faith carries the world's blessing
body: {{resolution}} is now the world's religion, and our own faith is the one it names. Our shrines will draw pilgrims from nations that once ignored them. The priests have one caution: a blessing is a loan, not a gift, and it is collected later.

variants.headline: The old faiths need no blessing
body: {{resolution}} now holds the chamber's blessing, and our own faith holds none of it. Our grandparents were named, wed and buried under the old rites, and not one of those days required a delegate's approval. A vote in a foreign hall cannot make a custom new again.

variants.headline: One altar blessed, many houses standing
body: To the editor: word has reached our street that the Congress chose {{resolution}}. My household keeps a different faith, as do the two houses beside mine. We lend each other tools and share one well, and no delegate has ever had to grant us leave. Let the chamber bless what it likes; the neighborhood will mind its own altars.

variants.headline: A sanctions proposal reaches the Congress
body: The World Congress is weighing {{resolution}}, a proposal to place a sanction on one nation. If it passes, the named country will find the chamber's doors closing wherever it does business. Every foreign office in the world has asked for a copy.

variants.headline: Sanctions: the chamber's weapon
body: {{resolution}} is on the chamber's table, and it points at one nation. A sanction is a war fought with shipping manifests: no soldier marches, but the named country loses trade, credit and friends. The delegates will choose a target as much as a tool. Let them remember that a rival keeps its own accounts, and settles them when the season turns.

variants.headline: Against the sanctions proposal
body: Delegates will soon vote on {{resolution}}. Before they do, let them ask what the named nation might still be willing to settle across a table, and what the rest of the world loses when that table is taken away. A boycott hardens the country it punishes. The Congress has more to gain from a rival at the table than from a rival in the cold.

variants.headline: Palaces aim it, markets feel it
body: The Congress is deciding on {{resolution}}, and the bill will land on the docks long before it lands in the history books. A sanction is drawn up by men in good coats and settled by men in aprons. The delegates should vote as if the fish market were watching, because it is.

variants.headline: A proposal to end a sanction
body: The World Congress is considering a motion to repeal {{resolution}}. If it passes, the censure lifts from the nation named in the text. Traders who lost business under it will wait for the harbor master's word before they trust the news.

variants.headline: A motion to lift {{resolution}}
body: The Congress will vote on repealing {{resolution}}. In a warehouse by the quay, a trader keeps a stack of orders she could not fill while the sanction held. If the vote goes her way, the letters go out that same evening.

variants.headline: The pressure may come off
body: The chamber is being asked to lift {{resolution}}, and no one has offered a reason that would survive a morning's argument. A sanction is the one hold the Congress has on the nation it names. Release it early and the whole lesson is lost. The delegates should keep their grip until the other side has earned the relief.

variants.headline: Sanction repeal on the docket
body: On the docket: repeal of {{resolution}}.
Status: proposed, vote pending, galleries restless.

variants.headline: Congress weighs limits on travel abroad
body: {{resolution}} is before the World Congress. If the delegates pass it, crossing from one country to another will take more time, more paper and more patience. Guesthouses and coaching yards that live on foreign custom are already counting the loss.

variants.headline: Travel limits proposed by {{proposer}}
body: {{proposer}} has brought {{resolution}} before the World Congress. If adopted, the measure would restrict travel among all the nations in the chamber. Near the arrivals gate, the guesthouse keeper is holding a list of rooms she dare not promise.

variants.headline: Will my cousins make it to the fair?
body: Sir, I had promised my cousins a place at our table for the autumn fair. They live beyond the border and have written to ask whether {{resolution}} will bar the road to them. Can your paper learn what the delegates actually mean to do? I can do without the fair. I would rather not do without my cousins.

variants.headline: The singer has two posters ready
body: With {{resolution}} still undecided, a touring singer paid for two print runs. One poster set advertises her foreign tour; the other names halls she could fill at home. The printer asked which to hang first. She chose the foreign run and stood looking at the ink.

variants.headline: A proposal to lift a travel ban
body: The World Congress will vote on ending {{resolution}}. A coaching innkeeper has taken the boards off the windows she shuttered when the ban began. She will not light the rooms until the count is in.

variants.headline: Notice: A proposal to end the travel ban
body: Word reaches us that {{proposer}} proposes to repeal {{resolution}}. Readers who hope to resume visits abroad should note that the restrictions stand until the chamber votes to lift them. Old arrangements are not restored by a proposal.

variants.headline: Give touring artists their audiences back
body: The chamber should repeal {{resolution}} and let the players travel again. A company that plays to half a house at home can fill a small hall across the water, and the takings keep the company together for another season. Keep the roads shut, and our stages will grow thin on the same few names.

variants.headline: Hear this, travelers: the ban may end
body: Travelers, hear this: the Congress may lift {{resolution}}. Pay no one who promises a quick passage until the vote is public. Money parted with at the dock is hard to recover at the border.
